status: read-only aggregation of existing completed observations; no new model/GPU/test
scope: Distinguish measured native64 task-gradient weakness from possible readout or joint-EOS-to-token decomposition causes. No production edit, scaling, baseline or entropy change.
native64_scope: Checkpoint25 native first8 prompts x original n8, one complete global64/local32/B4x8 minibatch. Four original backward passes, zero optimizer/scheduler updates. No historical bad update reconstructed.

success_token_advantages.interpretation: Different accepted estimators and distributions; these descriptive ratios are not a required equivalence, gradient norm identity or an official numerical failure criterion.

zero_return_scope.zero_dt_is_fixed_formula: G=0 gives A=G*(-expm1(-d))=0; not evidence of a dropped/incorrect action mask.
zero_return_scope.dilution: The native masked-mean still includes these long failure action tokens for entropy; this is a measured support difference from same-data original GRPO, not an attribution-only conclusion.

single_delete_existing_scope.identity_definition: (traj_uid, exact original_selected_input_ids, selected input position, token_id). Rank duplicates share identity; differing selected positions do not. This is identity counting, not independent statistical sampling.
single_delete_existing_scope.not_independent_sampling: Unique identities are not statistically independent samples; the original first minimum B4 selected token extrema, not random/population sampling.

v6_repeats.meaning: The same positive-extrema subset repeated three times, not 24 new distinct/independent probes.

supported: The full native64 minibatch has a much weaker DT task gradient than same-data original GRPO; original weighted entropy is dominant over this DT task gradient.
The native64 support difference includes 43 zero-return long failure trajectories versus 21 successful trajectories, alongside small successful-token DT advantages and signed cancellation.
For the selected local tokens, joint-response EOS decomposition does not equal direct single-token EOS model deletion, even when native joint endpoints replay almost identically.
Some selected joint credits are weaker than direct single deletion, while others are stronger; the existing sample does not establish uniform attenuation.
A one-token finite-versus-its-own-native-endpoint residual is separately recorded, so joint-span interaction alone cannot explain every selected discrepancy.
unknown: Population single-token deletion error rate or typical amplitude ratio across native64.
Whether, or what fraction of, the measured 0.00473187 DT/GRPO task-gradient norm ratio is caused by same-model return readout, joint-EOS decomposition, finite propagation or trajectory/support mix.
Reward-event readout calibration or exact environmental token-counterfactual values.
Whole-batch task-gradient change that replacing selected joint credits by direct single deletion would produce; no such original actor backward was measured.
Unique historical cause of TextCraft degradation or restored task performance.
method_preserved: Accepted token Q/V/A and original PPO remain unchanged. No credit normalization, scaling, new baseline, entropy tuning, whole-DT tolerance, correction or production implementation was proposed.
